title: Debugging: rule-author observability contract
preamble:
# Debugging: rule-author observability contract

The language-level contract for what a rule author
can see and do when diagnosing their rules — the sibling doc
to [LTES]. Where [LTES] describes how
behaviour is *asserted*, this doc describes how behaviour is
*understood*: interactively, with full inspection of engine
state, with time-travel through a session, with breakpoints on
the events that matter.

The integrator-facing surface that exposes it is
[NDBG] — the read-only engine APIs and the DAP mapping a DS debug
adapter serves them over. This doc is the
language-level commitment: every conforming runtime must expose
this surface, however it chooses to present it.

## What this is not

- Not an IDE or CLI spec. Concrete tools live with the
  reference runtime; other runtimes pick their own
  presentation.
- Not a re-statement of TESTING's introspection primitives.
  DEBUGGING builds on the same primitives but adds
  interactivity (step / pause / break) and navigability
  (walk backwards, diff two instants).
- Not a production-diagnostics spec. Debugging is a
  rule-author-time concern; production monitoring is runtime
  territory.
